background_story: Tadeo was a brilliant geologist who spent his life studying the Earth's crust. Growing up in a small village in Scotland, he was fascinated by the works of James Hutton, the father of modern geology. Tadeo's fascination with Hutton's theories on the Earth's formation led him to pursue a career in geology. He spent years researching and exploring the Scottish Highlands, uncovering new insights into the region's geological history. Tadeo's most significant discovery was a previously unknown fault line, which he named the 'Hutton's Ridge' in honor of his idol. His findings shed new light on the region's tectonic activity and earned him international recognition. Tadeo's work was a testament to the enduring legacy of James Hutton and the power of curiosity-driven exploration.
